title: Finite locally free descent admits invariant affine neighbourhoods
statement: Let $p:X\to Y$ be finite, flat, locally of finite presentation and surjective [def-pc-finite-locally-free], and let $V\to X$ have a transport descent datum $D$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Suppose every finite subset of $V$ lies in an affine open. Every point $v$ lies in an affine open $U\subseteq V$ contained in the inverse image of an affine open $B\subseteq Y$, and $U$ is transport-invariant: for every $T$, $f_1,f_2:T\to X$ with equal composites to $Y$, and $a:T\to V$ over $f_1$, if the image of $a$ lies in $U$, then the image of its transport to $f_2$ lies in $U$.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, Tags 0H8K and 03JE; Algebra, Tag 00DS

proof.text: Restrict to an affine neighbourhood B of the image of v in Y. The descent datum gives a scheme groupoid on V with finite locally free source and target maps, by base change of p. The orbit of v is finite. Place it in an affine open using the finite-subset assumption and shrink by finite prime avoidance into the inverse image of B.

Apply the norm construction of Tag 03JE on this restricted groupoid: remove the closed saturation of the complement, choose a function nonzero on the orbit and take the nonvanishing locus of its norm along the finite locally free source map. This gives an invariant affine open U containing v. Naturality identifies universal groupoid invariance with the displayed transport condition for arbitrary test schemes. No bound on the degree over all of Y is needed.

lean.statement: theorem exists_invariant_affine_neighbourhood {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {p : X ⟶ Y} [IsFinite p] [Flat p] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation p] [Surjective p] {V : Over X} (hV : ∀ s : Set V.left, s.Finite → ∃ U : V.left.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ s ⊆ U) (D : Over.DescentDatum p V) (v : V.left) : ∃ U : V.left.Opens, v ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ (∃ B : Y.Opens, IsAffineOpen B ∧ U ≤ (V.hom ≫ p) ⁻¹ᵁ B) ∧ ∀ {T : Scheme.{u}} (f₁ f₂ : T ⟶ X) (h : f₁ ≫ p = f₂ ≫ p) (a : Over.mk f₁ ⟶ V), Set.range a.left ⊆ U → Set.range (D.transport f₁ f₂ h a).left ⊆ U
